name: Convention with the Wea, 1809, and the Fort Wayne cession for the Kickapoo
aka: Treaty of Fort Wayne (1809), Article 9 and separate article
nations: Wea (now part of the Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma)
promises: Under Article 9 of the Fort Wayne treaty the tribes ceded a strip fifteen miles wide north-west of the Wabash on condition that the United States pay an annuity of $400 once the Kickapoo consented.
By the convention of 26 October 1809 the Wea gave their consent to the Fort Wayne treaty and its separate article, and the United States agreed to an allowance and annuity for them.
The Treaty of Greenville's terms on annuity payment and hunting on ceded land applied (Fort Wayne, Article 4).

breaches.what: The Indian Claims Commission found that Royce Area 73 (405,000 acres in the Wabash valley), ceded by the Wea under Article 9 of the Fort Wayne treaty and the Wea convention, was worth $1.40 an acre on 5 March 1810, and that the Wea received a $100 annuity worth $2,000 for it. It held the consideration for Areas 73 and 74 unconscionable and found the Wea entitled to $351,750 less the $2,000 credit.

breaches.what: For Royce Area 71, also covered by this entry, the Commission held the payments to the Wea ($7,500 for 549,081 acres) and to the Miami and Eel River unconscionable and awarded $678,900 to the Wea and $1,919,535.20 to the Miami and Eel River.

landTaken: Royce Area 73, 405,000 acres, and Royce Area 71, 2,095,688 acres, in Indiana and Illinois (Commission findings, 1969).
compensation: The Wea received a $100 annuity (valued at $2,000) for Area 73 and $7,500 in value for Area 71. The final Wea award under Docket 314-C, covering Areas 73 and 74, was $349,750 (28 January 1970); the Kickapoo award for the same two areas is recorded under kappler-112.
today: The Peoria Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma brought the Wea claims as successor to the Wea Nation.

nationVoice.summary: Chairman Lester Randall told the Senate in 2018 that the United States moved the Tribe several times, from Wisconsin through Illinois and Missouri to Kansas, under nine treaties made between 1809 and 1862, and that today the Tribe holds 4,859 acres in trust and 2,189 acres in fee within its 30 square mile reservation.

openQuestions: The queue gives this entry the same date as the Fort Wayne treaty (30 September 1809) with Royce Areas 73 and 71; which Kappler instrument Royce meant (the separate article with the Miami and Eel River, or the Wea convention of 26 October 1809) should be confirmed. The ratification and proclamation dates given are the Wea convention's.
A Peoria Tribe or Wea statement on this treaty was not found.
